63677-the-recluse.title: The Recluse
63677-the-recluse.creator: Unknown
63677-the-recluse.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In recent years he was always building. He had added a front porch to the cabin he had started with, then more rooms which he had never used, then an attic into which he never went. It had chairs and tables, a bed, a rug of vines, a garden for vegetables and tobacco, and a garden for flowers.

arxiv-1607-04074.title: Samvel Kh. Darbinyan
arxiv-1607-04074.description: Abstract Cycles of each even lengths in balanced bipartite digraphs Abstract Let D be a strongly connected balanced bipartite directed graph of order 2a\geq 4 . Let x,y be distinct vertices in D . \{x,y\} dominates a vertex z if x\rightarrow z and y\rightarrow z ; in this case, we call the pair \{x,y\} dominating.

arxiv-2011-10734.title: MultiShifter : software to generate structural models of extended two-dimensional defects in 3D and 2D crystals
arxiv-2011-10734.creator: Jon Gabriel Goiri, Anton Van der Ven
arxiv-2011-10734.description: Abstract Extended defects in crystals, such as dislocations, stacking faults and grain boundaries, play a crucial role in determining a wide variety of materials properties. Extended defects can also lead to novel electronic properties in two-dimensional materials, as demonstrated by recent discoveries of emergent electronic phenomena in twisted graphene bilayers.

arxiv-2106-07285.title: Probing Pre-Trained Language Models for Disease Knowledge
arxiv-2106-07285.creator: Israa Alghanmi, Luis Espinosa-Anke, Steven Schockaert
arxiv-2106-07285.description: Abstract Pre-trained language models such as ClinicalBERT have achieved impressive results on tasks such as medical Natural Language Inference. At first glance, this may suggest that these models are able to perform medical reasoning tasks, such as mapping symptoms to diseases. However, we find that standard benchmarks such as MedNLI contain relatively few examples that require such forms of reasoning.

arxiv-2306-12281.title: Quantum Fluctuation Theorem for Arbitrary Measurement and Feedback Schemes
arxiv-2306-12281.creator: Kacper Prech, Patrick P. Potts
arxiv-2306-12281.description: Abstract Fluctuation theorems and the second law of thermodynamics are powerful relations constraining the behavior of out-of-equilibrium systems. While there exist generalizations of these relations to feedback controlled quantum systems, their applicability is limited, in particular when considering strong and continuous measurements.

arxiv-2411-10235.creator: Arthur Stéphanovitch
arxiv-2411-10235.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Arthur Stéphanovitch. We extend the classical regularity theory of optimal transport to non-optimal transport maps generated by heat flow for perturbations of Gaussian measures. arxiv-2501-07826.title: Covariant analysis of electromagnetic current on the light cone: exposition with scalar Yukawa theory
arxiv-2501-07826.creator: Wenyu Zhang, Yang Li, James P. Vary
arxiv-2501-07826.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wenyu Zhang, Yang Li, James P. Vary. We present the first systematic investigation of the Lorentz covariance of the charge form factor for a strongly coupled scalar theory in (3+1)-dimensions. Our results are based on the first non-perturbative solution of the scalar Yukawa theory with a Fock sector expansion including up to thee-particles (one mock nucleon plus two mock pions or two mock nucleons plus one mock anti-nucleon). The light-front Hamiltonian is constructed and renormalized using a Fock sector dependent scheme.

arxiv-2505-08799.title: Measuring Security in 5G and Future Networks
arxiv-2505-08799.creator: Loay Abdelrazek 1 , Rim ElMalki 2 , Filippo Rebecchi 2 , Daniel Cho 1
arxiv-2505-08799.description: Abstract In today’s increasingly interconnected and fast-paced digital ecosystem, mobile networks, such as 5G and future generations such as 6G, play a pivotal role and must be considered as critical infrastructures. Ensuring their security is paramount to safeguard both individual users and the industries that depend on these networks.

arxiv-2505-13742.title: Understanding Task Representations in Neural Networks via Bayesian Ablation Thanks: Equal contribution; authors listed alphabetically
arxiv-2505-13742.creator: Andrew J. Nam, Declan Campbell, Thomas L. Griffiths, Jonathan D. Cohen, Sarah-Jane Leslie
arxiv-2505-13742.description: Abstract Neural networks are powerful tools for cognitive modeling due to their flexibility and emergent properties. However, interpreting their learned representations remains challenging due to their sub-symbolic semantics. We introduce a novel probabilistic framework for interpreting latent task representations in neural networks.

arxiv-2508-04552.title: Augmentation-based Domain Generalization and Joint Training from Multiple Source Domains for Whole Heart Segmentation
arxiv-2508-04552.creator: Franz Thaler, Darko Štern, Gernot Plank, Martin Urschler
arxiv-2508-04552.description: Abstract As the leading cause of death worldwide, cardiovascular diseases motivate the development of more sophisticated methods to analyze the heart and its substructures from medical images like Computed Tomography (CT) and Magnetic Resonance (MR). Semantic segmentations of important cardiac structures that represent the whole heart are useful to assess patient-specific cardiac morphology and pathology.

pmc-10607525.title: Steady-State and Time-Resolved Fluorescence Study of Selected Tryptophan-Containing Peptides in an AOT Reverse Micelle Environment
pmc-10607525.creator: Krystian Gałęcki, Agnieszka Kowalska-Baron, Katarzyna E Nowak, Anna Gajda, Beata Kolesińska, Mahmoud Ghomi, Santiago Sanchez-Cortés, Belén Hernández
pmc-10607525.description: The aim of this study was to demonstrate the utility of time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy in the detection of subtle changes in the local microenvironment of a tryptophan chromophore in a confined and crowded medium of AOT reverse micelles, which mimic biological membranes and cell compartmentalization.

pmc-10629675.title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived neural progenitor cells can be used to model effects of IL-6 on human neurodevelopment
pmc-10629675.creator: Kseniia Sarieva, Felix Hildebrand, Theresa Kagermeier, Zeynep Yentür, Katharina Becker, Simone Mayer
pmc-10629675.description: Maternal immune activation (MIA) increases the risks for neurodevelopmental disorders in offspring through inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-6 (IL-6). We therefore aimed to establish a human two-dimensional (2D) in vitro neural model to investigate the effects of IL-6 exposure on neurodevelopment. IL-6 signal transduction requires two receptors: interleukin-6 signal transducer (IL6ST) and interleukin-6 receptor (IL6R).

pmc-11517151.title: Vaccine conspiracy beliefs are the main determinant of adult vaccine hesitancy
pmc-11517151.creator: P Smola, U Zwierczyk, K Kowalska-Duplaga, M Duplaga
pmc-11517151.description: BackgroundMany factors influence the level of vaccine hesitancy. The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated that conspiracy beliefs are an important element of overwhelming misinformation. The main aim of the study was to assess the relationship between vaccine hesitancy (VH) and vaccine conspiracy beliefs (VCB) in Polish society.

pmc-11604666.title: mdCATH: A Large-Scale MD Dataset for Data-Driven Computational Biophysics
pmc-11604666.creator: Antonio Mirarchi, Toni Giorgino, Gianni De Fabritiis
pmc-11604666.description: Recent advancements in protein structure determination are revolutionizing our understanding of proteins. Still, a significant gap remains in the availability of comprehensive datasets that focus on the dynamics of proteins, which are crucial for understanding protein function, folding, and interactions.

pmc-11642332.title: Role of Acyl-CoA Thioesterase 7 in Regulating Fatty Acid Metabolism and Its Contribution to the Onset and Progression of Bovine Clinical Mastitis
pmc-11642332.creator: Bin Zhou, Bohao Zhang, Jiangyuan Han, Junjun Zhang, Jianfu Li, Weitao Dong, Xingxu Zhao, Yong Zhang, Quanwei Zhang, Margherita Maffei, Gaia Scabia
pmc-11642332.description: Clinical mastitis (CM) is a prevalent and severe inflammatory disease in dairy cows affecting the mammary glands. Fatty acid (FA) metabolism and associated enzymes are crucial for many physiological and pathological processes in dairy cows. However, the relationships among FA metabolism, FA-associated enzymes, and CM, as well as the mechanisms underlying their interactions, in dairy cows are not fully understood.

pmc-11657851.title: Marital happiness in a Middle Eastern context: are men happier?
pmc-11657851.creator: Manal Al Fazari, Mahmood Almaawali, Ehab Omara, Mustafa Ali Khalaf
pmc-11657851.description: BackgroundResearch on marital happiness in Middle Eastern cultures is lacking. This lack of understanding has created several challenges for policymakers and marriage counselors as divorce rates have increased over the past decade.MethodThis study aimed to assess the prevalence of marital happiness among Omani couples and its association with demographic variables, including gender, level of education, and duration of marriage.

pmc-11679521.title: Administration of Spermidine and Eugenol Demonstrates Anti-Tumorigenic Efficacy on Metastatic SW620 and Primary Caco-2 Colorectal Cancer Spheroids

pmc-11679521.description: The anti-cancer potential of eugenol (EUG) is well recognized, whereas that of spermidine (SPD) is subject to dispute and requires further research. The anti-tumorigenic potential of wheat germ SPD (150 µM) and clove EUG (100 µM), alone, in combination as SPD+EUG (50 µM + 100 µM) and, as a supplement (SUPPL; 0.

pmc-12730636.title: TRIM14 Regulation of Copper Homeostasis and Cuproptosis: A New Strategy to Overcome Chemoresistance in Glioblastoma
pmc-12730636.creator: Jianyong Wang, Enhao Zhang, Siqi Chen, Haifeng Wang, Yi Huang, Wenting Lan
pmc-12730636.description: Background: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Temozolomide (TMZ) remains the standard chemotherapy; however, its effectiveness is often hindered by the development of acquired resistance. Cuproptosis, a recently identified copper-dependent form of regulated cell death, has emerged as a potential therapeutic target.

pmc-13117438.title: A Segmentation-Assisted Three-Dimensional Planning Workflow for Static-Guided Pterygoid Implant Placement: A Proof-of-Concept Report
pmc-13117438.creator: Andra Patricia David, Silviu Brad, Laura-Cristina Rusu, Ovidiu Tiberiu David, Andra Ardelean, Marius Traian Leretter
pmc-13117438.description: Background/Objectives: Pterygoid implant placement represents a valuable alternative to conventional bone grafting procedures in the rehabilitation of the atrophic posterior maxilla; however, the procedure remains technically demanding because of limited visibility, difficult access, complex pterygomaxillary anatomy, and the need for precise angulation and distal bicortical anchorage.

pmc-13374664.title: Surgical experience with caseous calcification of the mitral annulus: a case report
pmc-13374664.creator: Kazuki Mori, Masato Morita, Eisuke Kawakubo, Masazumi Kume, Yuichi Nakazono, Takashi Shuto
pmc-13374664.description: Caseous calcification of the mitral annulus (CCMA) is a rare variant of mitral annular calcification associated with an increased risk of embolic stroke and diagnostic difficulty. We report a surgical case of CCMA that showed rapid enlargement after the initiation of hemodialysis.

pmc-13405975.title: Belongingness and School Refusal in Adolescents: Psychometric Validation and Identification of Risk Profiles
pmc-13405975.creator: María Pérez-Marco, Carolina Gonzálvez, Andrea Fuster, Ángel Amat, Alba Lorenzo-Rumbo, Graciela Arráez-Vera
pmc-13405975.description: Belongingness is a fundamental psychological need associated with adolescents’ emotional well-being, school engagement, and attendance. Despite the relevance of belongingness for adolescent adjustment, no validated measure of general belongingness is currently available for Spanish adolescents, and little is known about how different belongingness patterns relate to school refusal behaviour.

pmc-13424022.title: Experiences and Perspectives on Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Treatment in Mexico: A Subanalysis of the Diabetic Retinopathy Barometer Study
pmc-13424022.creator: Ingrid Y Pita-Ortiz, Raul Velez-Montoya, Marlon García Roa, Beatriz J Pérez Aragón, Luis F Rosales Rodríguez
pmc-13424022.description: IntroductionDiabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic macular edema (DME) are leading causes of vision loss worldwide and represent a growing public health concern in Mexico. Despite the availability of effective treatments, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies, adherence and persistence remain suboptimal, compromising outcomes.

pmc-13443748.title: Structural basis for selective and potent degradation of IRAK4 by KT-474
pmc-13443748.creator: Xue Fei, Anand Ramanathan, Caroline A. Daigle, Melissa Ford, Veronica Campbell, Xiaozhang Zheng, Mike Sintchak, Haoran Li, Hari Kamadurai, Richard Miller, Steven Kazmirski, Xin Huang, Matthew M. Weiss, Nello Mainolfi, Xiao Zhu

pmc-13509491.title: Diversity and Classification of the Actinopeptins: A New Family of Lanthipeptides Within the Genomes from the Phylum Actinomycetota
pmc-13509491.creator: Carlos García-Ausencio, Beatriz Ruiz-Villafán, Adelfo Escalante-Lozada, Martha Lydia Macías-Rubalcava, Romina Rodríguez-Sanoja, Sergio Sánchez
pmc-13509491.description: Background/Objectives: Lanthipeptides are post-translationally modified compounds and have broad industrial potential. Six distinct classes of lanthipeptides are defined by the biosynthetic enzymes that install lanthionine and β-methyl-lanthionine. Notably, class II lanthipeptides are modified by the LanM enzyme and are encoded by specific biosynthetic clusters found in both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

pmc-13526456.title: Validation of a Turkish Translation of the Stress in Emergency Healthcare Professionals: The Stress Factors and Manifestations Scale
pmc-13526456.creator: Halil Alsancak, Fatma Birgili
pmc-13526456.description: AimThe primary duties of emergency healthcare professionals (EHPs) are to provide emergency patient care to acutely ill and injured individuals. Due to the nature of their work, EHPs operate under constant stress, often requiring rapid decision‐making, swift action, and the delivery of necessary medical care in life‐or‐death situations, sometimes under inadequately safe conditions.
